Heapsort, step by step

Heapsort reads the array as a binary tree: index i has children 2i + 1 and 2i + 2. It first rearranges the array into a max-heap, where every parent is at least as large as its children, then moves the largest value to the end again and again.

Click the figure, then use ← →, space, Home and End, or the buttons.

How it works

  1. Build a max-heap: sift down every parent, from the last one up to the root.
  2. Sift down: swap a value with its larger child until both children are smaller.
  3. Swap the root, the largest value, with the last value in the heap. It is now in its final place.
  4. Shrink the heap by one and sift the new root down.
  5. Repeat until the heap has one value.

Cost

Time
O(n log n) in every case.
Space
O(1): it sorts in place.
Stable
No.

The code behind this figure

Nothing here is hand-animated. The figure comes from this code: a plain heapsort with stepthru tracer calls, such as compare and swap, that record each step.
